cim: Pasadena Church, Seminary to Hold Sunday AI Discussion as Five-Week Faith Course Concludes
cim_eredeti: Pasadena Church, Seminary to Hold Sunday AI Discussion as Five-Week Faith Course Concludes
szoveg_eredeti:
A Pasadena church is scheduled to conclude a five-week educational series on artificial intelligence Sunday, Oct. 25, bringing together questions about emerging technology, religious belief and the responsibilities of faith communities.

Lake Avenue Church lists the session for 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. in the Skyroom, Room 400 of Hutchins Hall, at 393 N. Lake Ave. The church’s event calendar identifies the course as “What Is AI and Why Does It Matter?”

The program is designed to help a general church audience understand artificial intelligence and consider its implications from a Christian perspective, according to the church’s announcement.

Lake Avenue Church introduced the five-week course in September as a partnership with Fuller Theological Seminary, also based in Pasadena. The church identified Dan Crichton, Finney Premkumar and Kutter Callaway among the speakers participating in the overall series.

The announcement did not identify which speakers would lead Sunday’s session.

The course reflects an effort to bring discussions about artificial intelligence beyond technical and academic settings and into religious communities, where questions about technology’s effects on human relationships, ethics and decision-making also arise.

Callaway, a faculty member at Fuller Theological Seminary, holds the William K. Brehm Chair of Worship, Theology, and the Arts and serves as associate professor of theology and culture. His academic interests include media, technology and the relationship between the church and contemporary culture, according to his university biography.

The collaboration follows an earlier Pasadena initiative addressing similar questions.

In October 2024, Lake Avenue Church organized the Infinity Summit at Fuller Theological Seminary. The conference brought together technology professionals, scholars and religious leaders to examine artificial intelligence and its ethical, philosophical and theological implications.

The summit’s agenda included discussions of artificial intelligence in health care, questions surrounding human agency and the possible role of religious institutions in responding to technological change.

The current course brings those broader issues into an educational format intended for a general church audience.

Sunday’s session is scheduled from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Lake Avenue Church, 393 N. Lake Ave., Pasadena. The church’s public event calendar does not specify whether new participants can register for the concluding session.

Additional information is available through the church’s website, lakeave.org, or by calling (626) 844-4700.
